fullPassage: One cannot validly argue that humans are morally superior beings on the ground that they possess, while others lack, the capacities of a moral agent. The reason is that, as far as moral standards are concerned, only beings that have the capacities of a moral agent can meaningfully be said to be either morally good or morally bad. Only moral agents can be judged to be morally better or worse than others, and the others in question must be moral agents themselves. Judgments of moral superiority are based on the comparative merits or deficiencies of the entities being judged, and these merits and deficiencies are all moral ones, that is, ones determined by moral standards. One entity is correctly judged morally superior to another if it is the case that, when valid moral standards are applied to both entities, the first fulfills them to a greater degree than the second. Both entities, therefore, must fall within the range of application of moral standards. This would not be the case, however, if humans were being judged superior to animals and plants, since the latter are not moral agents.

questions.passage: One cannot validly argue that humans are morally (A)[superior / inferior] beings on the ground that they possess, while others lack, the capacities of a moral agent. The reason is that, as far as moral standards are concerned, only beings that have the capacities of a moral agent can (B)[meaningfully / carelessly] be said to be either morally good or morally bad. Only moral agents can be (C)[judged / ignored] to be morally better or worse than others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 인간이 도덕적으로 우월한(superior) 존재라고 주장할 수 없다. 도덕적 행위자의 능력을 가진 존재만이 의미 있게(meaningfully) 도덕적으로 좋거나 나쁘다고 할 수 있다. 오직 도덕적 행위자만 판단될(judged) 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① superior — meaningfully — judged: 원문과 일치
❌ ② inferior(열등한): superior의 반의어
❌ ③ carelessly(부주의하게): meaningfully의 반의어
❌ ④ ignored(무시된): judged의 반의어
det.tip: superior = 우월한, meaningfully = 의미 있게, judged = 판단된

questions.passage: Judgments of moral superiority are based on the comparative (A)[merits / failures] or deficiencies of the entities being judged, and these merits and deficiencies are all moral ones, that is, ones (B)[determined / undermined] by moral standards. One entity is correctly judged morally superior to another if it is the case that, when valid moral standards are (C)[applied / denied] to both entities, the first fulfills them to a greater degree than the second.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 도덕적 우월성 판단은 비교 대상의 장점(merits)이나 결점에 기반한다. 이 장단점은 도덕적 기준에 의해 결정된(determined) 것이다. 도덕적 기준이 두 존재에 적용될(applied) 때 첫 번째가 더 충족하면 우월하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② merits — determined — applied: 원문과 일치
❌ ① failures(실패): merits의 반의어
❌ ③ undermined(약화된): determined와 다른 의미
❌ ④ denied(거부된): applied의 반의어
det.tip: merits = 장점, determined = 결정된, applied = 적용된

questions.passage: Both entities, therefore, must fall within the (A)[range / limit] of application of moral standards. This would not be the case, however, if humans were being judged superior to animals and plants, since the (B)[latter / former] are not moral agents. One cannot (C)[validly / falsely] argue that humans are morally superior beings on the ground that they possess the capacities of a moral agent.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 두 존재 모두 도덕적 기준 적용의 범위(range) 안에 있어야 한다. 동물과 식물은 도덕적 행위자가 아니므로 후자(latter)에 해당한다. 타당하게(validly) 주장할 수 없다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ range — latter — validly: 원문과 일치
❌ ① limit(제한): range와 유사하나 원문은 range
❌ ② former(전자): latter의 반의어
❌ ④ falsely(거짓으로): validly의 반의어
det.tip: range = 범위, the latter = 후자, validly = 타당하게

questions.passage: One cannot ①<u>validly</u> argue that humans are morally superior beings on the ground that they possess, while others lack, the capacities of a moral agent. The reason is that, as far as moral standards are concerned, only beings that have the capacities of a moral agent can ②<u>meaningfully</u> be said to be either morally good or morally bad. Only moral agents can be judged to be morally better or worse than others, and the others in question must be moral agents ③<u>themselves</u>. Judgments of moral superiority are based on the comparative merits or ④<u>strengths</u> of the entities being judged.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ strengths(강점) → deficiencies(결점): 도덕적 우월성 판단은 장점과 '결점'에 기반한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① validly(타당하게): 원문 일치
✅ ② meaningfully(의미 있게): 원문 일치
✅ ③ themselves(그들 자신): 원문 일치
❌ ④ strengths(강점): 원문은 deficiencies(결점) — 반의어로 교체됨

questions.passage: One entity is correctly judged morally ①<u>superior</u> to another if it is the case that, when valid moral standards are ②<u>applied</u> to both entities, the first ③<u>fulfills</u> them to a greater degree than the second. Both entities, therefore, must fall within the range of application of moral standards. This would not be the case, however, if humans were being judged superior to animals and plants, since the ④<u>former</u> are not moral agents.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ former(전자) → latter(후자): '동물과 식물'이 도덕적 행위자가 아니므로 '후자'가 맞다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① superior(우월한): 원문 일치
✅ ② applied(적용된): 원문 일치
✅ ③ fulfills(충족하다): 원문 일치
❌ ④ former(전자): 원문은 latter(후자) — 동물과 식물 = 후자
det.tip: the latter(후자) = animals and plants | the former(전자) = humans
